prs.title: Fix substring matches in WWW-Authenticate parsing
prs.author: Whning0513
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: extract_field_from_www_auth() in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py parses the WWW-Authenticate header with naive string/substring matching, which can mis-parse parameter values (e.g. commas inside quoted strings, or substrings matching a param name). Both PRs replace this with a quote/escape-aware tokenizer that splits the header on top-level commas. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: extract_field_from_www_auth() in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py parses the WWW-Authenticate header with naive string/substring matching, which can mis-parse parameter values (e.g. commas inside quoted strings, or substrings matching a param name). Both PRs replace this with a quote/escape-aware tokenizer that splits the header on top-level commas. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: 3041's _split_www_authenticate_segments() splits the entire header (not just the substring after the first space) on top-level commas, then _extract_bearer_auth_params() walks the resulting segments to detect where a new auth-scheme starts (via partition on the first space) and collects only the params belonging to the Bearer challenge. This handles a header containing multiple challenges (e.g. 'Basic realm=x, Bearer realm=y'). 3012's _iter_www_auth_params() finds only the first space in the whole header and treats everything after it as one flat, single-scheme param list, so it would incorrectly merge params from a second challenge into the first if more than one scheme is present in the header.

prs.title: Fix pre_parse_json corrupting str | None values that look like JSON
prs.author: vientooscuro
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json() in func_metadata.py over-aggressively calls json.loads() on string field values when the field's annotation is a Union containing str (e.g. `str | None`, `str | int`), corrupting plain string inputs that happen to look like JSON (numbers, booleans, objects/arrays) instead of passing them through as strings. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json() in func_metadata.py over-aggressively calls json.loads() on string field values when the field's annotation is a Union containing str (e.g. `str | None`, `str | int`), corrupting plain string inputs that happen to look like JSON (numbers, booleans, objects/arrays) instead of passing them through as strings. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs add a helper to pre_parse_json to skip JSON pre-parsing for str-containing unions, but #3056's `_is_optional_str` explicitly calls `_unwrap_annotated()` on each union member before comparing to str, so `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` (the idiomatic form for a described optional string parameter) is correctly detected and left unparsed. #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` compares union members directly against a `_SIMPLE_TYPES` frozenset (`arg not in _SIMPLE_TYPES`) with no Annotated-unwrapping step, so an Annotated-wrapped str member fails that membership check and the field is still incorrectly routed through json.loads — i.e. #2032 does not fix the bug for the common `Annotated[str, Field(...)]` case. #3056 also scopes the change narrowly to str|None (documented in its own docstring), avoiding a behavior change for other simple-type unions like str|int or str|bool that #2032's broader fix silently alters.

prs.author: app/claude
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: OAuth authorization-server metadata (oauth_metadata) only lives in memory, so after a process restart / cold start, _refresh_token has no way to know the token endpoint, breaking silent token refresh. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: OAuth authorization-server metadata (oauth_metadata) only lives in memory, so after a process restart / cold start, _refresh_token has no way to know the token endpoint, breaking silent token refresh. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: 2492 fixes this by adding get_oauth_metadata/set_oauth_metadata to the TokenStorage protocol and persisting metadata to storage, which requires every TokenStorage implementation to adopt new methods and can serve stale endpoint data if the AS later rotates its configuration. 3263 instead triggers on-demand discovery before a cold-start refresh, adds an issuer-binding check to validate the rediscovered metadata actually belongs to the expected authorization server (closes a mix-up risk 2492 doesn't address), and tracks an eager_discovery_attempted flag so servers publishing no metadata aren't re-probed on every refresh — all without changing the TokenStorage interface.

clusters.pick_reason: 3041's _split_www_authenticate_segments() splits the entire header (not just the substring after the first space) on top-level commas, then _extract_bearer_auth_params() walks the resulting segments to detect where a new auth-scheme starts (via partition on the first space) and collects only the params belonging to the Bearer challenge. This handles a header containing multiple challenges (e.g. 'Basic realm=x, Bearer realm=y'). 3012's _iter_www_auth_params() finds only the first space in the whole header and treats everything after it as one flat, single-scheme param list, so it would incorrectly merge params from a second challenge into the first if more than one scheme is present in the header.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs add a helper to pre_parse_json to skip JSON pre-parsing for str-containing unions, but #3056's `_is_optional_str` explicitly calls `_unwrap_annotated()` on each union member before comparing to str, so `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` (the idiomatic form for a described optional string parameter) is correctly detected and left unparsed. #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` compares union members directly against a `_SIMPLE_TYPES` frozenset (`arg not in _SIMPLE_TYPES`) with no Annotated-unwrapping step, so an Annotated-wrapped str member fails that membership check and the field is still incorrectly routed through json.loads — i.e. #2032 does not fix the bug for the common `Annotated[str, Field(...)]` case. #3056 also scopes the change narrowly to str|None (documented in its own docstring), avoiding a behavior change for other simple-type unions like str|int or str|bool that #2032's broader fix silently alters.

clusters.pick_reason: #2395's change is scoped entirely to the max-attempts branch of `_handle_reconnection`: it builds a JSONRPCError keyed to the specific pending request's id and sends it via `ctx.read_stream_writer.send`, unblocking only that one call while the rest of the session/task group keeps running. #3098 addresses the same branch by raising `StreamableHTTPError` out of the task group (via a new recursive `_unwrap_exception` helper that digs through ExceptionGroups), which tears down the whole client session instead of failing just the pending request, and its diff also changes an unrelated import (`from __future__ import annotations as _annotations` -> `from __future__ import annotations`), widening the change's footprint in a file that two other unrelated PRs (#1674, #3092) are also touching. The smaller, request-scoped diff in #2395 is less likely to conflict with those parallel changes.

clusters.pick_reason: 2492 fixes this by adding get_oauth_metadata/set_oauth_metadata to the TokenStorage protocol and persisting metadata to storage, which requires every TokenStorage implementation to adopt new methods and can serve stale endpoint data if the AS later rotates its configuration. 3263 instead triggers on-demand discovery before a cold-start refresh, adds an issuer-binding check to validate the rediscovered metadata actually belongs to the expected authorization server (closes a mix-up risk 2492 doesn't address), and tracks an eager_discovery_attempted flag so servers publishing no metadata aren't re-probed on every refresh — all without changing the TokenStorage interface.

clusters.pick_reason: 3041's _split_www_authenticate_segments() splits the entire header (not just the substring after the first space) on top-level commas, then _extract_bearer_auth_params() walks the resulting segments to detect where a new auth-scheme starts (via partition on the first space) and collects only the params belonging to the Bearer challenge. This handles a header containing multiple challenges (e.g. 'Basic realm=x, Bearer realm=y'). 3012's _iter_www_auth_params() finds only the first space in the whole header and treats everything after it as one flat, single-scheme param list, so it would incorrectly merge params from a second challenge into the first if more than one scheme is present in the header.
